newsitem.title: UK: HEAVY RAIN HALTS SW ENGLAND GRAINS HARVEST.
newsitem.headline: HEAVY RAIN HALTS SW ENGLAND GRAINS HARVEST.

text.p: Heavy rain has halted the cereals harvest in south-western England for the time being, farming sources said.
Localised flooding was predicted, a spokesman for the Meteorological Office said. There had been heavy rain throughout the region, except for Cornwall, on Wednesday morning, he said.
South Wales was also affected. The rain was moving north-eastwards, he said.
"It's probably the wettest it's been (at harvest time) since 1968," a spokesman for the National Farmers' Union in the region said.
Farmers were already suffering from the lowest prices for 20 years and the adverse impact of excessive wet weather on quality could mean a further hit for incomes, he complained.
Normally harvesting in the region would have reached a natural break by now, after oilseed rape and winter barley were finished, he said. But there remained some to get in.
And farmers were watching the quality of wheat deteriorate. "It's going from gold to brown. It's when it turns black you really have to start worrying."
Normally the region gets more than the average rain and wet summers are not usually unwelcome but a farmer said that "you can have too much of a good thing."
